solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: He wooed many, initially counting as a star

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word counting

parts.note: a nova is a star that suddenly flares in brightness

explanation.surface: A man with many romantic conquests is listed among the stars of the show.
explanation.definitionFit: Giacomo Casanova was the famous Venetian seducer, so his name stands for any prolific lover of women.

clue.text: A politician visiting key American college grounds

indicators.note: visiting means one piece goes to stay inside the other pair of pieces

parts.note: C is a musical key
MP is a Member of Parliament, a British politician

explanation.surface: A politician drops in on an important American university site.
explanation.walkthrough: 'key' looks like an adjective meaning important, but it is the musical key C.
explanation.definitionFit: A campus is the land and buildings belonging to a university or college.

clue.text: Practise on undertaker's vehicle

parts.note: re means on or concerning, as in business letters
a hearse carries the coffin at a funeral

explanation.surface: Someone does a trial run in a funeral car.
explanation.definitionFit: To practise something before performing it is to run through it in advance, a synonym.

clue.text: Floating structure right behind

parts.note: aft means at or towards the back, especially of a ship

explanation.surface: A floating platform with something just to the right and behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: A raft is a flat platform of logs or planks lashed together that floats on water.

clue.text: Musical carrier's device for securing locks?

parts.note: Hair is the famous 1960s rock musical
a grip is a travelling bag, a carrier for belongings; the 's stands for is, linking to the definition

explanation.surface: A theatrical bag-carrier owns a gadget for fastening locks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'locks' suggests doors and keys, but here means hair; the question mark flags that pun.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairgrip is a small clip that holds locks of hair in place.

clue.text: A large tree growing on high mountains

parts.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
a pine is a common coniferous tree

explanation.surface: A big tree flourishes high up in the mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpine plants are those found growing in high mountain regions, above the tree line.

clue.text: Unhappy about new seaside feature

indicators.note: about means the first word wraps around the second

parts.note: sad means unhappy

explanation.surface: Someone is miserable about a fresh development at the beach.
explanation.definitionFit: Sand covers beaches, so it is a typical feature of the seaside.

clue.text: Prevent an area producing fruit

parts.note: to ban something is to prevent it

explanation.surface: An order to stop a region growing its crops.
explanation.definitionFit: A banana is a long curved tropical fruit, so this is an example of the class.

clue.text: Blooming action required in tiddly-winks!

definitions.meaning: a mild British intensifier, like bloody or ruddy
in the game of tiddlywinks counters are made to jump by pressing on their edges

explanation.surface: An exasperated remark about the movement needed in a children's counter game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blooming' looks floral, but it is the mild British expletive. Tiddlywinks is a game of pinging small discs into a cup.
explanation.definitionFit: Both 'blooming' and the answer are mild British swearwords; the second sense is the tossing motion of the game.

clue.text: Complain, parking at east end of estate, perhaps

indicators.note: in an across clue the east end is the right-hand side, so the parking letter goes after

parts.note: an estate is a type of car, hence perhaps
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles about parking in the eastern part of a housing estate.
explanation.walkthrough: An estate car is the British name for a station wagon.
explanation.definitionFit: To carp is to find fault or grumble persistently, a synonym of complain.

clue.text: Info supplied by senior officer, briefly

indicators.note: briefly says the word is cut short, keeping only its start

parts.note: a general is a high-ranking army officer

explanation.surface: Information handed over by a senior officer in a short briefing.
explanation.walkthrough: GEN is also the common abbreviation for general.
explanation.definitionFit: Gen is British informal slang for information or details.

clue.text: Customer's urn comes adrift

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, linking the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: adrift means loose and out of place, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A shopper's tea urn floats away.
explanation.definitionFit: A consumer is a person who buys goods or services, the same as a customer.

clue.text: Look after chief, popular with army

parts.note: main means chief or principal
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: Taking care of a leader who is well liked by the troops.
explanation.definitionFit: To maintain something is to keep it in good condition, to care for it.

clue.text: Half of them taking degree? That's novel

indicators.note: half of picks out two of the four letters of them, here the back pair

parts.note: MA is a Master of Arts degree

explanation.surface: Half of the group taking a degree: a new idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like an adjective meaning new, but it is the noun: a book.
explanation.definitionFit: Emma is Jane Austen's novel, so the definition is a general term with this as an example.

clue.text: Cannibal's mother — of tidier appearance

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, linking the definition to the wordplay

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
neater means more tidy-looking

explanation.surface: A cannibal's mother looks smarter than her son.
explanation.definitionFit: A man-eater is a person or beast that eats human flesh, which a cannibal does.

clue.text: Motorway circling a large West African country

indicators.note: circling means the first piece goes round the others

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's first major motorway, written as MI
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A motorway runs around a sizeable country in West Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 runs from London to Leeds; the figure 1 is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Mali is a landlocked nation in West Africa, its capital Bamako.

clue.text: Sneak attending class?

definitions.meaning: to sneak is to tell tales on someone to authority
a form is a school class, so being present in it is being ...

explanation.walkthrough: 'Sneak' looks like creeping about; in British school slang it means telling tales. Form is the British word for a school class or year group.
explanation.definitionFit: Telling tales to authority is passing on information; read as two words, it means being present in class.

clue.text: Lofty declaration of model at work?

definitions.meaning: lofty means grand and impressive in size or manner
a model striking poses for the camera might announce what they are doing as ...

explanation.walkthrough: Split as I'M POSING, the answer becomes what a modelling job's sitter would say.
explanation.definitionFit: Something grand and impressive in appearance is lofty or stately, a synonym.

clue.text: Conflict associated with trouble for Cockney spouse?

definitions.text: associated with trouble for Cockney spouse?
definitions.meaning: in Cockney rhyming slang trouble and ... means wife, so this word goes with trouble

explanation.walkthrough: Cockney rhyming slang replaces a word with a rhyming phrase: 'trouble and strife' means wife, the London East End's best-known example.
explanation.definitionFit: Strife is bitter disagreement or fighting; it is also the partner of trouble in the rhyming phrase.

clue.text: News about union leader's sister?

indicators.note: about says the first piece wraps around the second

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for new, and news is read as the plural, two of them

indicators.note: leader's points to the first letter of union

explanation.surface: Reports concerning the head of a trade union's sister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sister' looks like a sibling; the question mark marks it as a religious sister.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman in a religious order is addressed as Sister, so the definition is by example.

clue.text: Pudding ingredient originally steamed in the past

indicators.note: originally points to the first letter of the word steamed

parts.note: ago means in the past

explanation.surface: A dessert component that used to be cooked by steaming in earlier times.
explanation.definitionFit: Sago is a starch from palm pith, used to make a milk pudding.

clue.text: Very young child born in creek

indicators.note: in says the first letter goes inside the other word

parts.note: a bay or creek is an inlet of the sea
B is the abbreviation for born, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: An infant born in a small inlet.
explanation.definitionFit: A baby is an infant, a very young child.

clue.text: Some are altogether genuine

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some people are entirely authentic.
explanation.definitionFit: Genuine and real both mean authentic, not fake, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Girl embraced by parents in TV programme

indicators.note: embraced by means the girl's name is held within the parents

parts.note: pa and ma are informal words for father and mother
Nora is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A daughter hugged by her mother and father in a television show.
explanation.walkthrough: Panorama is the BBC's long-running current affairs programme.
explanation.definitionFit: The BBC's flagship investigative current affairs series has this title, so the definition is by example.

clue.text: Strike in snack bar?

definitions.meaning: to strike is to hit or knock about, as waves do
a counter or café serving light meals, as in a station refreshment room

explanation.surface: A walk-out at the café counter.
explanation.definitionFit: To buffet is to strike repeatedly; a buffet is also a counter selling food on trains or in stations.

clue.text: Pig chap always used for celebration

parts.note: a hog is a pig
a chap is a man
ay, also spelt aye, is a poetic word for always

explanation.surface: A pig and a man are always used at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: Hogmanay is the Scottish New Year's Eve celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scots' New Year's Eve party is a particular celebration, so the definition is by example.
